summary: Taito's police-pursuit racing and vehicular-combat series, beginning with the 1988 arcade hit and expanding into gunplay, first-person chase sequels, handheld entries, and spin-offs.

entries.title: Chase H.Q.
entries.definitive_edition: Original arcade release plus Genesis/Mega Drive vehicle variation

emulation.notes: Use arcade emulation for the primary; use Genesis emulation only for its alternate vehicles.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade output with optional 16-bit version-specific content

primary.version: Original Taito Z System arcade release
primary.why: Chase H.Q. was designed for Taito Z System arcades with sprite-scaling road presentation and branching pursuit routes. The many computer, console, handheld, and compilation releases are ports or access routes; the Genesis/Mega Drive version has alternative player vehicles, so that port is secondary for its exclusive variation only.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version in MAME/original hardware; use Genesis/Mega Drive only to sample its alternate player vehicles.

secondary.exclusive_content: Genesis/Mega Drive release titled Chase H.Q. II/Super H.Q. includes minor changes such as alternative player vehicles.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the alternate player vehicles after the arcade primary.
secondary.why: Arcade is the fidelity route; this port has sourced version-specific vehicle changes.

entries.remaster_caveats: Genesis/Mega Drive Chase H.Q. II/Super H.Q. is a version of the first game, not the 2007 arcade sequel Chase H.Q. 2.

entries.title: Special Criminal Investigation

emulation.notes: Use arcade emulation for the primary route.

primary.version: Original Taito Z System arcade release
primary.why: Special Criminal Investigation is the arcade sequel to Chase H.Q., adding gunfire from the passenger seat and new pursuit design. Home computer and console versions are ports, while the Saturn release is an arcade-emulation bundle.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version in MAME/original hardware; use Saturn only as a Japan-only compilation route if owned.

entries.remaster_caveats: Amstrad Plus/GX4000 version was written but not released commercially.

entries.title: Crime City

emulation.notes: Use arcade emulation or hardware for the primary route.

primary.why: Crime City is a Chase H.Q. spin-off that shifts from third-person driving to side-scrolling shooting. It is an arcade spin-off, with no home platform route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version in MAME/original hardware if supported.

entries.remaster_caveats: Spin-off rather than a driving sequel.

entries.title: Quiz H.Q.

emulation.notes: Use arcade emulation or hardware; Japanese-language trivia may be a practical barrier.

primary.why: Quiz H.Q. is a Japan-only Taito quiz spin-off based on Chase H.Q., using the Chase officers and pursuit framing for trivia play. No sourced home port is identified.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese arcade version in MAME/original hardware if supported and language needs are acceptable.

entries.remaster_caveats: Quiz spin-off; not translated in the cited public source.

entries.title: Super Chase H.Q.

emulation.notes: Use arcade emulation for the primary route.

primary.version: Super Chase: Criminal Termination arcade release
primary.why: Super Chase H.Q. began as the arcade game Super Chase: Criminal Termination, using updated Taito hardware and switching the series to a first-person cockpit view. The SNES and Game Boy releases are home/handheld adaptations.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version in MAME/original hardware; use SNES or Game Boy only for home-version comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Arcade title is Super Chase: Criminal Termination; home releases use Super Chase H.Q.

entries.title: Chase H.Q.: Secret Police

emulation.notes: Use accurate Game Boy Color emulation or hardware.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Accurate Game Boy Color output with modern scaling

primary.why: Chase H.Q.: Secret Police is a Game Boy Color installment with chase sequences and a strategy layer for assigning detectives on a map. It has only one sourced release platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Game Boy Color version in SameBoy, mGBA, Analogue Pocket, or original hardware.

entries.remaster_caveats: Handheld strategy/vehicular-combat installment, not an arcade port.

entries.title: Chase H.Q. 2

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / Taito Type X2 preservation setup
emulation.notes: Use original hardware where possible; public emulation status may vary.

primary.version: Original Taito Type X2 arcade release
primary.why: Chase H.Q. 2 is the 2007 arcade sequel developed with Gamewax, using 3D graphics on Taito Type X2 hardware. It is distinct from the Genesis/Mega Drive port named Chase H.Q. II.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original arcade hardware or a legally configured Taito Type X2 preservation setup if available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not confuse this 2007 arcade sequel with the Genesis/Mega Drive release named Chase H.Q. II/Super H.Q.
